newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Dev interim solid - analysts.
newsitem.headline: New World Dev interim solid - analysts.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd's interim results were solid and the company was on the way to a strong full year, analysts said on Tuesday.
The Hong Kong property developer said it had net profit of HK$2.2 billion in the six months ended December 31, well up on HK$1.7 billion for the previous corresponding period.
The result was in line with expectations, said Daiwa Institute of Research analyst Eric Yuen, adding he was optimistic about the company's prospects.
"Looking forward we are looking for very strong property sales in both 1997 and 1998," he said.

Analyst Nicholas Wong of James Capel noted that New World's interim result did not rely on exceptionals -- the previous corresponding period's figure of HK$1.7 billion included HK$1.1 billion in exceptional gains.
"The outlook is extremely bright both in Hong Kong and in China," said Wong.

Yuen expected good contributions from a Sheung Wan office complex near Hong Kong's busy Central district on Hong Kong Island, and from Discovery Park, a 50 percent joint venture in the New Territories with HKR International Ltd.
He expected phases II and III of Discovery Park to contribute HK$3 billion to full-year net profits in the 12 months to June 30, 1998.

Yuen forecast that the Sheung Wan office project would contribute another HK$4 billion in net profits in 1998, although the company may choose not to book all that income that year since it would be difficult to sustain such growth in 1999.

New World Development is a property investment and development company, whose activities also span hotels, infrastructure, television entertainment and telecommunications, construction, civil engineering and estate management.
Subsidiary New World Infrastructure Ltd on Tuesday reported net interim profits to December of HK$273.42 million, from HK$213.47 million.
New World Development shares ended the day at HK$43.20, up HK$0.30 on Monday's close.
